kids-mental-health.name: Kids' mental health
kids-mental-health.line: I see more kids anxious and depressed, and too little help for them.

sources.passage: The percentage of students overall who had persistent feelings of sadness or hopelessness (42% to 40%).
The percentage of female students who felt persistently sad or hopeless (57% to 53%) … who seriously considered attempting suicide (30% to 27%).

four-in-ten U.S. parents with children younger than 18 say they are extremely or very worried that their children might struggle with anxiety or depression at some point. In fact, mental health concerns top the list of parental worries, followed by 35% who are similarly concerned about their children being bullied
Depression and anxiety are among the leading causes of illness and disability among adolescents.

kids-mental-health.prevalence: 40% of U.S. high school students had persistent feelings of sadness or hopelessness, down from 42% (CDC Youth Risk Behavior Survey); among female students, 27% seriously considered attempting suicide. Four-in-ten parents are extremely or very worried their children will struggle with anxiety or depression (Pew).

bullying.name: Bullying
bullying.line: I see kids bullied at school and online, and the adults around them not stopping it.

sources.passage: The percentage of students overall who were bullied at school (15% to 19%).

four-in-ten U.S. parents with children younger than 18 say they are extremely or very worried that their children might struggle with anxiety or depression at some point. In fact, mental health concerns top the list of parental worries, followed by 35% who are similarly concerned about their children being bullied

bullying.prevalence: 19% of U.S. high school students were bullied at school, up from 15% (CDC Youth Risk Behavior Survey); 35% of parents are extremely or very worried their children will be bullied (Pew).

guns-and-kids.name: Guns and kids
guns-and-kids.line: I'm afraid kids will get shot, at school or anywhere else.

sources.passage: Overall, 57% of teens say they are worried about the possibility of a shooting happening at their school, with one-in-four saying they are very worried.
Parents of teenagers express similar levels of concern as teens themselves, with 63% saying they are at least somewhat worried about the possibility of a shooting happening at their child’s school.
the child firearm death rate increased 68%, exceeding motor vehicle crashes in 2020 to become the leading means of death among children ages 1-19
The percentage of students overall who missed school due to safety concerns either at school or on the way to school (9% to 13%).
The percentage of students overall who were threatened or injured with a weapon at school (7% to 9%).
Black and Hispanic parents are more likely than White and Asian parents to say they are extremely or very worried about their children getting shot or getting in trouble with the police.

guns-and-kids.prevalence: 57% of U.S. teens and 63% of their parents were at least somewhat worried about a shooting at school (Pew). Firearms became the leading means of death among children ages 1-19 in 2020 (America's Health Rankings). 13% of high school students missed school due to safety concerns, up from 9% (CDC YRBS).

child-poverty.name: Child poverty
child-poverty.line: I see kids going without the basics because their families can't afford them.

sources.passage: Children in poverty US 11,445,000 17% 2019 16% 2023 BETTER
Children living in high-poverty areas US 5,546,000 10% 2014–18 8% 2019–23 BETTER
Children whose parents lack secure employment US 18,437,000 26% 2019 25% 2023 BETTER

child-poverty.prevalence: 16% of U.S. children lived in poverty in 2023, 11,445,000 children; 25% had parents who lacked secure employment (KIDS COUNT Data Book).

child-abuse.name: Child abuse
child-abuse.line: I see kids hurt or neglected by the adults who should be protecting them.

sources.passage: Out of those referrals, 546,159 children were found to be victims of abuse or neglect.
An estimated 2,000 children died as a result of abuse or neglect in 2023, a rate of 2.73 children per every 100,000.

FAM3.B Child maltreatment: Percentage of substantiated maltreatment of children ages 0–17 by maltreatment type and age, 2023. Overall: Neglect 74.0; Physical abuse 17.5; Sexual abuse 9.8; Psychological abuse 6.9

child-abuse.prevalence: 546,159 U.S. children were found to be victims of abuse or neglect, and an estimated 2,000 children died as a result of abuse or neglect in 2023 (HHS, via USAFacts). Neglect was 74.0% of substantiated cases (childstats.gov).

foster-care.name: Foster care
foster-care.line: I see kids in foster care moved from home to home, and many turn 18 with no family at all.

sources.passage: 70,418 U.S. foster children were waiting to be adopted at the end of 2024
15,379 Youth aged out of foster care without a permanent family in 2024

foster-care.prevalence: 70,418 U.S. foster children were waiting to be adopted at the end of 2024, and 15,379 youth aged out of foster care without a permanent family that year (National Council For Adoption, from AFCARS).

childcare-shortage.name: Finding childcare
childcare-shortage.line: I see families who can't find a childcare or preschool spot anywhere near them.

sources.passage: finds that a majority, or 51 percent, of Americans live in neighborhoods classified as child care deserts.
Young children (ages 3 and 4) not in school US 4,317,000 52% 2014–18 54% 2019–23 WORSE

childcare-shortage.prevalence: 51 percent of Americans live in neighborhoods classified as child care deserts (Center for American Progress); 54% of U.S. children ages 3 and 4 were not in school in 2019–23 (KIDS COUNT).

teens-no-path.name: Teens adrift
teens-no-path.line: I see young people out of school and out of work, with nothing pulling them forward.
aliases: Young people not in school or work

sources.passage: Teens not in school and not working US 1,168,000 6% 2019 7% 2023 WORSE

teens-no-path.prevalence: 7% of U.S. teens were not in school and not working in 2023, up from 6% in 2019, about 1,168,000 teens (KIDS COUNT Data Book).

kids-unsafe-online.name: Kids online
kids-unsafe-online.line: I worry about strangers reaching kids online to exploit them.

sources.passage: In 2025, the CyberTipline received 21.3 million reports

The CyberTipline received 1.4 million reports concerning online enticement in 2025, which included more than 800 reports in which an offender traveled to meet a child in person and more than 80,000 reports concerning sextortion

kids-unsafe-online.prevalence: The National Center for Missing & Exploited Children's CyberTipline received 21.3 million reports in 2025, including 1.4 million concerning online enticement and more than 80,000 concerning sextortion.

kids-health.name: Kids' health
kids-health.line: I see kids growing up on junk food, with too little time to run around.

sources.passage: Children and teens (ages 10 to 17) who are overweight or obese US N.A. 31% 2018–19 31% 2022–23 SAME

kids-health.prevalence: 31% of U.S. children and teens ages 10 to 17 were overweight or obese in 2022–23 (KIDS COUNT Data Book).

moms-and-babies.name: Pregnancy and birth
moms-and-babies.line: I see moms and babies not getting the care they need before and after birth.

sources.passage: Low birth-weight babies US 308,263 8.3% 2019 8.6% 2023 WORSE
Complications from pregnancy and childbirth are among the leading causes of death for girls aged 15–19 years globally.

moms-and-babies.prevalence: 8.6% of U.S. babies were born at low birth weight in 2023, up from 8.3% in 2019 (KIDS COUNT Data Book). Worldwide, complications from pregnancy and childbirth are among the leading causes of death for girls aged 15–19 (WHO).
